summary: The G and 2D differences are laser heating, not a change in strain or doping. G moves from 1581.14 to 1579.28 cm-1 (-1.86 ± 0.12) and 2D from 2669.32 to 2664.17 cm-1 (-5.15 ± 0.13) between 0.5 and 5 mW, and both lines broaden. Si is stable to 0.05 cm-1, so it is not calibration. The shifts match the supported-graphene temperature coefficients for a rise of about 115 to 150 K. Trust the 0.5 mW spectrum for strain and doping, as an upper bound on the cold position, and do not use the 5 mW one. At 0.5 mW the sample looks near-neutral, nearly strain-free, defect-free (no D peak) and monolayer-like, but this is qualitative at 532 nm.

observations.finding: G and 2D downshift and broaden with laser power; this is laser heating.
Calibration or drift is excluded as the cause of the shifts.
observations.evidence: Si line 520.86 / 520.90 / 520.91 cm-1 (offsets +0.17 to +0.21 from 520.7), a scatter of 0.05 cm-1 versus shifts of 2 to 5 cm-1. Si does not shift downward, so only the graphene is hot.

observations.finding: The shifts are consistent with a thermal rise of roughly 115 to 150 K between 0.5 and 5 mW.
observations.evidence: -1.86 cm-1 / -0.016 cm-1/K gives about 116 K from G; -5.15 / -0.034 gives about 151 K from 2D; the two agree within about 30%. Coefficients are for supported monolayer graphene measured between 83 and 373 K, so this is an extrapolation. The 2D shift per mW is non-linear: about -2.1 cm-1/mW between 0.5 and 2 mW and about -0.7 cm-1/mW between 2 and 5 mW.
observations.source: Calizo et al. 2007, arXiv 0708.1223, Table I p.7

observations.finding: Doping is excluded as the cause of the power dependence.
observations.evidence: Delta2D/DeltaG = 2.8 ± 0.2, whereas the hole-doping direction has slope 0.70. G broadens with power, while doping narrows G. The 2D/G height ratio is constant (G/2D height 0.366, 0.363, 0.372).
observations.source: Lee et al. 2012, Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (arXiv 1209.0234, p.5); Das et al. 2008, Nat. Nanotechnol. 3, 210

observations.finding: Strain cannot be separated from heating by slope alone, but it is unlikely to be the cause.
observations.evidence: The strain slope 2.2 ± 0.2 is close to the observed 2.8 ± 0.2, and the heating slope is about 2.1 from Calizo. A static strain would not change reproducibly with laser power, and no G+/G- splitting is seen. Substrate thermal-expansion strain is part of the heating response.
observations.source: Lee 2012, Fig. 2; Ferrari and Basko 2013, Nat. Nanotechnol. 8, 235, p.20

observations.finding: At 0.5 mW the sample is near-neutral and nearly strain-free (qualitative, 532 nm).
observations.evidence: G 1581.14 cm-1 is within 0.5 cm-1 of the Lee origin 1581.6; 2D 2669.3 cm-1 is near the origin shifted to 532 nm (2676.9 minus about 8, from about 100 cm-1/eV dispersion, which is uncertain by about 3 cm-1). FWHM(G) 13.4 cm-1 is the low-doping value.
observations.source: Lee 2012 p.4; Ferrari and Basko 2013 p.7; Cancado 2011 Nano Lett. 11, 3190

observations.evidence: No D peak above baseline (1300 to 1400 cm-1 maximum is at baseline level in all spectra). 2D is one Lorentzian of FWHM 26 cm-1, consistent with 1L on SiO2 (above 22 cm-1) and far narrower than turbostratic (about 50 cm-1). 2D/G height ratio is 2.7, below 4, which is not discriminating without the SiO2 thickness.
observations.source: Ferrari 2006, PRL 97, 187401 p.2-3; Neumann 2015, Nat. Commun. 6, 8429, Fig. 1h; Yoon 2009, PRB 80, 125422

caveats: The shift errors are fit statistics only; add about 0.2 to 0.3 cm-1 for calibration. The conclusions hold at that level.

The Lee 2012 strain/doping decomposition is validated only at 513 to 516 nm, for hole doping. At 532 nm the 2D reference position is shifted by an approximate dispersion (about 100 cm-1/eV), so the near-neutral, nearly strain-free statement is qualitative.

Thermal coefficients from Calizo 2007 are for 83 to 373 K on a particular substrate. Extrapolating to the temperatures reached here, and treating G and 2D separately, gives only an estimate of 115 to 150 K.

The 2D shift is sublinear in power, so a simple linear extrapolation to zero power is unreliable. Even 0.5 mW is probably somewhat heated, so the 0.5 mW positions are upper bounds for the cold G and 2D.
The spectra were taken in increasing power order. Irreversible laser-induced desorption, annealing or doping changes cannot be excluded without a repeat at 0.5 mW.

The 5 mW spectrum has a marginal feature near 2318 cm-1 (FWHM 33 ± 14, position error ±4), not interpreted. The fit also reports a broad background centred near 2554 cm-1 (FWHM 535), probably luminescence or background.
The 2D/G ratio of 2.7 is below 4, which is not discriminating without the SiO2 thickness (interference changes it by hundreds of percent). A small doping contribution is not excluded.
The area/power increase of about 12% with power is unexplained (focus, coupling or thermal change).
questions_for_user: Was a 0.5 mW spectrum retaken after the 5 mW exposure? If it matches the first, the changes were reversible heating and not laser-induced desorption, annealing or doping.
What is the SiO2 thickness? It sets the expected 2D/G intensity ratio (Yoon 2009), and the observed 2.7 is below the textbook 4.
Is the stated power measured at the sample, and what is the spot size? This is needed to scale heating.
What are the exfoliation and anneal history and the environment (air or vacuum)? They bear on the doping origin and on what the laser does to the surface.
What are the spectral resolution and calibration practice? Si FWHM is about 3.4 cm-1, but I assumed a calibration uncertainty of 0.2 to 0.3 cm-1.

limits: No quantitative strain or doping values are given. The G-2D vector relation is not valid at 532 nm, and heating contaminates all three spectra.
The data cannot give the true graphene temperature, the cold (zero-power) G and 2D positions, or the sign of any residual doping.
Static strain cannot be distinguished from thermal-expansion strain from the shifts alone; polarization-resolved G, a second laser, or a power series extrapolated to zero would be needed.
Data start at 450 cm-1, so the low-frequency shear modes (relevant for bilayer) are not observable. Layer number rests on the 2D line shape and width only.
Second-order and combination bands (such as LO+ZO') were not analysed; the analysis covers G, 2D, D and Si only.
